question.problem: The arrivals of vehicles at a crossing occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one every $10$ seconds. Determine the probability that the next vehicle will arrive at the crossing at least $5$ seconds after the previous vehicle's arrival. Round your answer to four decimal places.

current_example.problem: At a clothing store, customers purchase clothes for newborns continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one sale every $30$ minutes. What is the probability that it takes more than $60$ minutes to sell the next set of newborn clothes?
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the purchases occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next purchase as an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134435/assets/49fa146efc8029727469bc5909c2a946c9cb96383976d4096d455b423a428479.svg)

Let $X$ be the amount of time until the next set of newborn clothes is sold. Since there is a purchase every $30$ minutes on average, the rate is $\lambda =1/30$ purchases per minute.

The time intervals between successive purchases can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =1/30,$ and we can write 

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( \dfrac{1}{30} \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134435/assets/c883b4eb685b0ec0f7a9742bc274e518e8d60abe8ea7e5367c95dab7665fb8a8.svg)

Therefore, the probability that it takes more than $60$ minutes to sell the next set of newborn clothes is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 60) & ={\int }_{60}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{60}^{\infty }\frac{1}{30}{e}^{-x/30}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-x/30}|}_{60}^{\infty } \\  & =-{e}^{-\infty }+{e}^{-2} \\  & =0+{e}^{-2} \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.1353.\end{aligned}
$$
